name: Charles Elliott House

dates.altered: 'Some of the interior elements were remodeled between 1790 and 1800 in the Adamesque style' (Wikipedia).
dates.note: The build date is the node's own ('Circa 1759'); the Wikipedia article read gives the 1764 purchase of the property for 2,500 pounds current currency and no construction date. Recorded as the node states it, and marked so.

refs.title: Charles Elliott House - Wikipedia
refs.note: 'The house is a Georgian double house built of cypress with interior cypress woodwork ... Although the house follows the normal floorplan for a double house (four rooms per floor separated by a hall and staircase), the rear rooms are much smaller than the front rooms; the disparity in sizes has even led to the house's being described as a "modified Charleston single house." Unusually, the house has thick brick firewalls rising from the basement to the attic between the rooms to limit the spread of any fires.'

note: Written 4 Sep 2026 from the WP-11.1 research pass. The exemplar name and location the charleston-single-house node already carried were kept exactly. Worth carrying, and it is why this exemplar has no standing: the one source read calls this a DOUBLE house of the four-room plan, described as a 'modified Charleston single house' only because its rear rooms are small -- against the node's exemplar note, which calls it 'among the earliest documented single houses, showing the plan fully resolved'. Nothing here is changed; the disagreement is recorded for a ruling. No HABS record and no individual register page were found.
